title: Media pipeline can double-claim pending items under concurrent runs
reasoning: The guard that skips when a processing item exists and the later pending-item claim are separate read-then-write operations. If two run_media_pipeline tasks start together, both can observe no processing item, then both can select the same pending row before either commits the status change, causing duplicate transcription/summarization work and racing final status/content writes.
recommendation: Claim work atomically. Use a conditional update from pending to processing keyed by item id/status in one transaction, then proceed only if one row was updated; also consider a process-wide or database-backed media-pipeline lock.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests start two media pipeline runs concurrently or assert that only one worker can claim a pending MediaItem.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create one pending MediaItem, run two _process_pending_items tasks concurrently with a delayed MediaProcessor, and assert process() is called once and only one run records the item as processed.
